experiment: E2 — does the lattice amplification A link two independently measured lengths?
question: The dimensionless, wavelength-free lattice output A = a_med/g* must satisfy A = 2*pi*lambda/D if the lattice wave is light and the grain diameter is D. Both lambda and D are measured independently; A comes only from the simulation. Does A_req = 2*pi*lambda/D fall inside the uncertainty of the simulated A?

inputs_measured.lambda_source: I2-stabilised HeNe 633 nm line (CIPM recommended value), = realization_lock lambda_ref

data.note: No new simulation is run. E2 re-analyses the existing, previously published SOC outputs (N=200, g0=2e-7, k_nn=12, original defaults, unchanged). Not blind: the run summaries (A_median) were seen before this registration; the statistic and criterion below were fixed without re-reading the per-avalanche data.
data.inclusion: all rows with finite A_post > 0; no burn-in cut, no best-avalanche selection

statistic.primary: median of pooled A_post (run3 seed 2 + indep seed 11)
statistic.uncertainty: 95% percentile interval of the median from event-level bootstrap, 10000 resamples, numpy default_rng(19)
statistic.why_event_level: only two seeds exist, so a seed-cluster bootstrap is not meaningful; this is stated as a limitation

criterion.PASS: A_req lies inside the 95% bootstrap interval of the pooled median

also_reported: pull of A_req relative to the pooled median in units of the bootstrap half-width
relative width of the interval (the resolving power of this test)
known_limits: A scales as N^(-1/3)/g0; the test is conditional on the original N=200, g0=2e-7 settings, which are fixed here and not tuned
